To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

2D fitting can be used to determine the macromolecular resonance baseline in 1H MRS of the brain based on a range on complementary spectra, not relying on smooth assumptions or global assumptions on the T1 relaxation time.

2D fitting can be used to determine the macromolecule (MM) baseline in 1H MR spectroscopy (MRS) based on a combination of inversion recovery (IR) and two-dimensional (2DJ) separation spectra, and that 2DJ-2D fitting including IR and 2D spectra is expected to provide a more robust MMBL in cases with more variability in data quality or lipid resonance overlap.

we have developed a new method to determine the macromolecule signal in 1H MR spectroscopy of the brain based on 2D fitting of inversion-recovery (T1) and 2D-J separation (T2) spectra, and that the method is more robust than previous methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general fitting tool for interrelated data arrays, which can be used to solve a wide range of problems in biomedical MR imaging and spectroscopy.
a new approach to determine the MMLB in MR spectra.
the application of 2D linear combination model fitting in the context of the determination of the MMBL in MR spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
2DJ-IF is the best option, but that IR-only is a good alternative.
2D fitting is a powerful tool to determine the MBL in clinical MR spectra.
2D fitting is a powerful tool that may improve the quality of MMBL determination in MR spectra.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2D-Fitting approach in FiTAID is a promising alternative to existing methods for determination of MMBL in clinical 1 H MRS.
2DJ-2D fitting is a robust and versatile tool for MMBL determination.
the 2DJ method has the potential to be the most robust, the IR the simplest, and the 2DJ-2IR method the best compromise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2DJ-IF can be applied to a wide range of applications where linear-combinations of interrelated datasets are advantageous.
2D model fitting of inter-related datasets can be used to solve problems in MR spectroscopy that are not easily solved with 1D model fitting.
linear-combination models can be applied to interrelated datasets to obtain more reliable results.
